patch.value: GH-781: managed built-in extensions redeclare public SDK contracts locally, and the mirrors already disagree with the authoritative declarations in shipped packages

GH-781.

The managed built-in extensions statically import the public SDK and then redeclare the SDK's own contracts locally. The local mirrors are already out of agreement with the authoritative declarations, and because these files ship inside published packages, a downstream repository cannot correct them in place.

Reported evidence against published 2026.7.27:

- builtin-todos-import-export declares listAllItemMetadata with three parameters. The authoritative SDK declaration takes five, the last four optional, and builtin-guide-shell legitimately passes all five. Two built-ins therefore disagree about the same function.
- builtin-todos-import-export and builtin-beads-import each duplicate LocatedItem rather than importing the exported SDK type.
- builtin-templates locally mirrors TemplatesSaveResult, TemplatesListResult and TemplatesShowResult although the public SDK exports all three.

Why this matters beyond tidiness: the project's stated architecture is that the CLI and every package are thin layers over one public SDK. A local mirror is a second, undeclared definition of a public contract. It compiles, so no gate objects, and it drifts silently until a signature change makes the mirror wrong at runtime. The three-versus-five parameter disagreement is that drift already having happened. Because the artifacts are package-managed, the blast radius is every consumer of the published package, and the repair cannot be done downstream.

The fix is structural rather than per-file: built-ins must consume the exported SDK types, and a parity gate must fail when a package redeclares a type or function signature the SDK already exports. Without the gate this recurs the moment a new built-in is written, which is the same pattern as the unnecessary-spread findings that were closed as a class and then re-reported in a new file.

Scope is type and signature mirroring inside managed built-ins plus the gate that keeps it fixed. The unreachability of SDK command-authoring primitives is a different defect with its own owner and is the reason authors reach for mirrors in the first place, so it is recorded here as an upstream cause rather than folded in.

Managed built-in extensions import listAllItemMetadata, LocatedItem, TemplatesSaveResult, TemplatesListResult and TemplatesShowResult from the public SDK instead of redeclaring them; A parity gate fails when a package-owned file redeclares a type or function signature that the public SDK already exports; The listAllItemMetadata arity disagreement between builtin-todos-import-export and builtin-guide-shell is resolved against the authoritative five-parameter declaration; The gate runs against the packaged artifacts so a drifted mirror cannot be published; GH-781 is closed with the parity gate named as the control that keeps it closed
